Subject: Your lab notes, and a confession

Trisha,

Congratulations on topping the structures test again. Honestly, when the list went up my stomach dropped, and I sulked in the canteen for about an hour. Then I remembered you had asked for my beam-deflection notes on Friday. For a moment I thought about "forgetting" to send them. They are attached now, with the diagrams. Since first year, your marks have made me start revision two weeks earlier than I ever used to, and my own scores have climbed because of it. I still plan to beat you in the final semester 🙂 so keep working.

Ojas

qa.q: Which test did Trisha top again?
qa.a: Trisha topped the structures test again.

qa.q: What was Ojas feeling when the list went up, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Ojas felt hurt and competitive; the stomach dropped and the sulking in the canteen for about an hour show it.

qa.q: What could Ojas do to keep this rivalry useful in the final semester?
qa.a: Ojas could keep starting revision early and keep sharing notes, treating Trisha's marks as a standard to reach rather than something to block.

qa.q: How might Trisha read this email?
qa.a: Trisha may find it honest and generous, since Ojas admitted the sulking yet still sent the notes that were asked for. 🙂

grounding: A classmate rival pushes the writer's standard while the writer stays decent by sending the notes.

passage: Eshaan and Tejas had traded first and second rank at their Pune engineering college since the first semester, and everyone in the lab knew it. The night before the robotics demo, Eshaan found Tejas's team notebook left open on the shared bench, with the password for their test rig written on the cover. For a long moment he just looked at it. One changed line and their robot would stall in front of the judges. Instead he closed the notebook and texted Tejas: 'You left your stuff on bench 3. Password's on the cover, might want to hide it.' Then he went back to his own robot and rewrote the turning function a third time, because Tejas's arm had looked smoother than his in the trial. At the demo, Tejas's team won by two points. Eshaan shook his hand and asked how they had tuned the arm.

qa.q: On which bench did Tejas leave the notebook?
qa.a: Tejas left the notebook on bench 3.

qa.q: What was Eshaan feeling as he looked at the open notebook?
qa.a: Eshaan felt tempted and tense, the rivalry pulling toward sabotage, before he chose to close it.
Warning Tejas and putting the energy into his own turning function, because it kept him decent and actually raised his standard.

qa.q: How might Tejas see Eshaan's text about the notebook?
qa.a: Tejas would likely be surprised and grateful, seeing his rival as someone who competes fairly.

grounding: Shows a long rivalry where the temptation to sabotage is refused and the rival instead pushes Eshaan to improve his own work.

'Just shelve the constitutional law volume in the wrong section,' Anmol whispered. 'Disha needs it tonight for her memorial.'
'No.'
'Dhruv, she beat you in the last two moots.'
'I know exactly how many times she beat me.' Dhruv pulled the volume off the shelf himself. 'Which is why I'm reading it first, properly. Then I'm putting it back.'
Later, at the library door, Disha caught up with him. 'Heard you were in the reference section for three hours.'
'Couldn't let you walk in with better arguments again.'
She laughed. 'Your rebuttal last time was good, by the way. I stole the structure.'
'Then I'm stealing your opening. Fair?'
'Fair. See you Friday.'
Anmol shook his head. 'You two are strange.'
'She makes me better,' Dhruv said. 'That's the whole point of her.'

qa.q: What did Anmol suggest doing with the volume?
qa.a: Anmol suggested shelving it in the wrong section.

qa.q: How does Dhruv feel about Disha beating him?
qa.a: Dhruv feels stung and competitive, keeping count of every loss, but he respects her and wants to beat her fairly.

qa.q: What would you advise someone tempted the way Dhruv was?
qa.a: Refuse the sabotage and put the energy into preparing better, as Dhruv did by reading the volume first and putting it back.

qa.q: How does Disha seem to see the rivalry?
qa.a: Disha treats it as friendly and useful, openly borrowing Dhruv's rebuttal structure and laughing about it.

grounding: Shows a rival refusing a friend's sabotage idea and using the competition to lift his own preparation while staying decent.
